faq.a: Cumhur is associated with the Arabic form جُمْهُور, whose core sense is cumhur; the public, multitude (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Cumhur?
faq.a: Cumhur is associated with Arabic. Cumhur is the Turkish form of Arabic جُمْهُور (Jumhūr), meaning 'the public, multitude'.
Yes — the underlying form جُمْهُور is Arabic.
Cumhur can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Cumhur should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Jumhūr is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Cumhur mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Cumhur is rendered جمہور and carries the sense جمہور، عوام.

faq.q: What does Cumhur mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Cumhur is rendered جمهور and carries the sense جمهور، توده.
A romanized syllable approximation is cum-hur. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Cumhur?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Cumhur, cumhur. Script forms are جمهور, جمہور, جُمْهُور, जुम्हूर.

faq.q: Is Cumhur a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
